page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.medium is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the ARMv9 architecture. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 1 dedicated vCPU mapped directly to 1 physical Neoverse-V2 core operating at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB of RAM, adhering to the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory general purpose ratio. The instance lacks local storage, depending entirely on remote EBS volumes, and does not include GPU acceleration. Baseline network throughput is configured at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the expected profile of a single-core instance. Single-threaded metrics show competent baseline efficiency, scoring 1,746.0 in single-core Geekbench and reaching 14.21 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, which places in the upper quartile of evaluated systems. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression performs around the median at 30.11 GB/sec. However, with only a single thread available, overall multi-core throughput scores such as the multi-core Geekbench score (1,746.0) and multi-core stress-ng CPU test (1,692.68) rank in the bottom decile across cloud instances. Large block uncached memory bandwidth registers at 30.44 GB/sec for reads and 11.67 GB/sec for writes.

Given its minimal core count and modest memory capacity, m8gn.medium delivers resource efficiency primarily for lightweight, bounded workloads where higher multi-threaded capacity is unnecessary. Database operations recorded 1,503.76 on PassMark, while Redis SET throughput achieved 2.26 million operations per second. Static web serving reached 2.57 GB/sec. The instance is suited for microservices, lightweight web servers, entry-level caching nodes, testing environments, and background queue workers that rely on ARM64 infrastructure.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine utilizing an ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU), 4.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and does not supply local storage, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate respectable single-thread efficiency, including an average Geekbench single-core score of 1,746.0 and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.21 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics rank in the lowest tier due to the presence of only a single core. With 2.26 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.57 GB/sec static web throughput, m8gn.medium is suited for lightweight microservices, testing environments, low-traffic web serving, and small-scale caching layers.
